title: RBAC & API key rotation: journey mapping, wireframes, and proposals
body:
Purpose: capture proposed UX flows for org/team role management + API key/service account rotation + audit log correlation. This is a working doc: contains wireframe text sketches, journey maps, prioritized backlog, open questions. Aim: align on minimal viable flows for Q2 launch (hosted + dedicated customers), then iterate for Private.

Context / problem statement:
- Many customers ask for stronger defaults around key rotation and clearer RBAC visibility.
- Current console has role list + keys page (flat). Hard to answer: who has access via service account X, when was key rotated, and what calls used that key.
- Need unified mental model: roles are policies attached to identities (users, service accounts, teams). Keys are credentials tied to identities and appear in audit logs as auth tokens. We need first-class UX to trace from role -> identity -> key -> audit events.

Goals (must-haves):
1) Make it simple for org admins to audit "who can access model inference" for a given resource (model, route).
2) Provide safe, discoverable key rotation workflows (manual + auto-rotate schedules) with rollback and service impact estimation.
3) Offer quick answers in console: "Which keys used this model in the last 30 days?" and "Which identities have editor/viewer roles on this team?"
4) Keep flows consistent between org-level and team-level pages; avoid duplication.

Non-goals (out of scope for MVP):
- Full RBAC policy DSL editor (we'll surface roles & presets only).
- Automatic code-change integration for key updates (we'll offer notifications and playbooks).

Personas:
- Org admin (security/compliance): needs auditable trails, export, and policy enforcement.
- Platform engineer (SRE for internal apps): needs safe rotation with minimal downtime and a way to test rotated keys in staging.
- App developer (product engineer): wants simple service account creation and keys for automated jobs; needs to find expired keys quickly.

Journey map (happy path + edge cases):
1) Org admin wants to confirm a third-party integration stopped access after a role revocation.
   - Page entry points: Org -> Security -> Access Overview OR Model -> Access -> View callers
   - Wireframe: access-overview panel with 'policy search' (free text), 'recent access by resource' (list), left rail filter by team/org/resource
   - Action: click a resource -> right pane shows identities with roles, keys associated, last-used timestamp, link to audit events
   - Edge: service account used via ephemeral key (no long-lived key). Show 'ephemeral' badge and TTL.

2) Platform engineer rotates a key used by background job.
   - Entry: Org -> Service accounts -> SA name -> Keys tab
   - Wireframe: key list shows key id, created, last-used, status (active/pending-rotation/disabled), rotation policy pill
   - Flow: create new key -> toggle 'staged' (create but do not disable old), copy new secret to clipboard (masked), run smoke test button triggers a test run (calls internal test endpoint)
   - If smoke test passes, admin clicks 'promote' which marks old key as disabled and new key as primary. Console prompts: "Estimated impact: X routes will see 403 for keys not updated" (estimate based on last 30-day traffic by key)
   - Fallback: if fail, 'revert' button re-enables old key and notes in audit log

Wireframe text sketches (desktop-focused, 1200px layout):
- Top-level: "Access" landing page
  - Left column (240px): filters (scope: org/team/model), role presets, search
  - Middle (main): list of resources (models, routes, buckets) with inline summary: active callers, outstanding keys older than 90d, last audit event
  - Right (context panel): detail for selected resource -> identities table (identity | type | role | keys | last used | revoke)

- Service account detail
  - Header: SA name, owned-by-team, created-at, TTL (if ephemeral)
  - Tabs: Overview | Keys | Activity (Audit log) | Notes
  - Keys tab: table with Key ID, Status, Created, Last used, Rotation policy, Actions (create-stage, promote, disable)
  - Create key modal: name, expiry, staging toggle, allow-console-copy checkbox, add test-caller endpoint (optional)

Permission inheritance & matrix (textual):
- Roles: Owner > Admin > Editor > Viewer. Team-level roles inherit to resources within team namespace.
- Service accounts get assigned team-scoped roles OR resource-scoped roles. If a service account belongs to multiple teams, effective permission is union.
- Overrides: explicit deny not in MVP.

Audit log UX & correlation
- Requirements: free-text search (user, key id, request id), time range, resource type, outcome (200/403/500), and correlation by trace id/request id.
- Wireframe: Activity tab in SA -> timeline grouped by day. Each event rows shows timestamp, actor (user/key/sa), action (model.invoke), route, response status, linked request id -> clicking opens modal with full event JSON + related events (same request id across services)
- Advanced: quick filter buttons: "keys older than 90d", "inactive > 60d", "failed auth in last 24h"

Design decisions (provisional):
- Show 'last-used' metric for keys based on audit logs; if no matching events -> show 'never used'.
- Provide a 'staging' state for keys to avoid forced swap; staging keys allowed for up to 7 days by default.
- Key promotion is a two-step action (promote -> confirm). Promotion writes audit event and triggers notification to owners.
- Default rotation policy suggestion: 90 days for long-lived keys; ephemeral keys default TTL 24h.
- We will NOT show secrets in full after initial creation (only masked) — provide 'create + copy' only once warning.

Accessibility & mobile notes:
- Mobile: collapse left filters into top picker. Context panel becomes full-screen detail view. Keep smoke-tests and promote actions reachable with primary CTA.
- Keyboard-first: table rows must support arrow navigation and keyboard action keys (D = disable, S = stage new key)

Backlog (prioritized, rough JIRA mapping):
1) RB-101: Access overview page + resource->identities panel (acceptance: search by resource, view identities, export CSV) - target: Q2 alpha
2) RB-102: Service account detail + keys CRUD + staged key UX (acceptance: create staged key, copy secret once, run smoke-test) - target: Q2 beta
3) RB-103: Audit log correlation for keys (acceptance: search by key-id -> list events, open event modal) - target: Q2 beta
4) RB-104: Key rotation estimation engine (uses last-30d events to estimate impacted routes) - spike then implement Q3
5) RB-105: Rotation schedule UI (auto-rotate) + notification preferences - low priority

Acceptance criteria examples (RB-102):
- Create key flow: admin can create a staged key and copy secret exactly once. The key appears in UI as status 'staged' and is not primary.
- Smoke test: clicking 'run smoke test' sends a test request and returns pass/fail within 30s; UI shows logs in modal.
- Promote: promoting staged key updates primary and write audit log event; old key status becomes 'disabled'.

Open questions / risks:
- How accurate is the "estimated impacted routes" calculation if customers use many ephemeral tokens? Need telemetry spike.
- Do we allow API token rotation for Third-party OAuth integrations? Those map differently to service accounts.
- Legal: what retention policy for audit logs? Need to align with compliance team (tag: legal-retention).

Notes to engineering/infra:
- Audit log correlation requires storing request-id on inference path; if not present, consider deterministic hashing to correlate.
- Smoke-test endpoint should be rate-limited and only allowed for keys with appropriate scopes (prevent abuse).
- Need backend support for staged keys and promote endpoint; consider idempotency tokens for promote action.

Next steps (short-term):
- UX: create 2 visual mockups (desktop list/detail + SA keys modal) and tie to RB-101/102 tickets. Owner: Miguel.
- PM: confirm retention requirement with compliance. Owner: Dana.
- Eng infra: spike to compute last-30d per-key route usage. Owner: Evan.

Appendix: quick checklist for design review
- [ ] Show 'last used' for keys (where available)
- [ ] Mask secret after creation; provide copy-once
- [ ] Add staged-state with promote/revert flows
- [ ] Add audit events for create/promote/disable actions
- [ ] Export CSV for access overview

Draft sign-off: feedback requested from SRE and Security by 2025-03-11. Please add comments inline or ping in #console-access on Slack.

"Notes to self": keep the RBAC model simple for MVP; prioritize detective capabilities (audit + trace) over preventive (deny) until we have usage patterns that require more complex policy language.

Payload examples (for engineers):
- Promote payload: POST /api/v1/service-accounts/{sa}/keys/{key_id}/promote {body: {promote_reason: string, request_id: uuid}}
- Smoke-test: POST /internal/test-keys {key_id, test_route}

End of doc.
